narrativeReportMd:
# ChargeItemDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ChargeItemDefinition` is present in R4 but absent from the R6 ballot package. That is a hard breaking change for any R4 instance whose `resourceType` is `ChargeItemDefinition`, because an R6 validator or generated model set has no resource definition to accept it.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 resource StructureDefinition with the R6 package, including the R6 index and related financial artifacts. No same-name or clearly renamed R6 resource-level successor was found. `Invoice`, `DeviceDefinition.chargeItem`, and the new `MonetaryComponent` datatype provide partial charge/price surfaces but do not retain canonical definition lifecycle, applicability rules, or reusable property groups.

## Main migration themes
The dominant issue is artifact removal, not a narrow element-level delta. R4 data cannot be validated as R6 without a non-core extension/profile strategy or a domain-specific transform into another resource. Price component values can sometimes be moved to `MonetaryComponent`, but this is not a lossless resource conversion and has terminology caveats such as R4 `deduction` being folded into R6 `discount` semantics.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the missing R6 resource identity. It affects validation, parsers, generated classes, canonical references, package indexes, and any server capability that used the R4 resource.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for migration design because the local computable package does not provide an official successor, ConceptMap, or StructureMap. Review is especially needed before mapping R4 applicability expressions and property groups into R6 invoices or device billing structures.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because `ChargeItemDefinition` was draft and FMM 0 in R4, removal may be justified by specification evolution. A less disruptive option would have been to keep a deprecated R6 resource or publish an official cross-version mapping, but the supplied local inputs do not show that such a compatibility path exists.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analyses should cover any R4 `ChargeItemDefinition-apply` operation, ChargeItemDefinition search parameters, and related financial resources or datatypes used as migration targets.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ChargeItemDefinition` appears to have been removed from the R6 core package. Existing R4 instances, canonical references, generated classes, and resource-specific APIs need explicit migration handling; the main uncertainty is whether HL7 intends a specific replacement path not visible in the local computable package.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily an artifact-retirement problem. Systems should inventory persisted `ChargeItemDefinition` instances and canonical references, decide whether to preserve them in an R4 island/custom profile, or map selected business content into R6 resources such as `Invoice`, `DeviceDefinition`, and `MonetaryComponent`. Applicability expressions, canonical lifecycle metadata, and reusable property groups do not have an obvious lossless R6 target.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R6 package lacks `ChargeItemDefinition`: the assigned file is absent, the R6 index contains no matching entry, and exact package search found no references. Confidence is medium for replacement analysis because local package artifacts do not include official ballot narrative, Jira rationale, or cross-version maps.

findings.title: ChargeItemDefinition resource is absent from the R6 core package

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete ChargeItemDefinition resource.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `ChargeItemDefinition` is a concrete, non-abstract `DomainResource` specialization with required `url` and `status` elements and a local content model for billing-code definitions, applicability criteria, and price components.

newState.summary: R6 has no ChargeItemDefinition StructureDefinition or package index entry.
newState.narrativeMd: The assigned R6 file is absent, and the R6 package index contains no resource, operation, search parameter, or other artifact whose id, filename, URL, or type includes `ChargeItemDefinition`.

facts.note: The assigned R6 StructureDefinition path is absent.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: A direct same-canonical match is impossible because the R6 StructureDefinition is absent. Exact text search for `ChargeItemDefinition` in the R6 package found no references, so there is no local evidence of a rename, split, or merge preserving identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break: a resource instance with `resourceType: "ChargeItemDefinition"` is valid against the R4 core package but has no R6 core StructureDefinition to validate against. Runtime impact is high for parsers, generated model libraries, REST servers, package index lookups, and canonical resolution logic that expect every resource type to exist in the target FHIR version.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource is draft/FMM 0 and likely rare, but it represents billing rules and price applicability; silent loss or misinterpretation can affect financial correctness.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire or replace a draft financial definition resource whose R4 description explicitly said it provided only a rough structure requiring profiling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain ChargeItemDefinition in R6 core as a deprecated or informational resource while steering new work to other financial structures.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of retiring a draft, FMM 0 financial definition resource is reasonable, especially because the R4 definition says it only provides a rough structure that requires profiling. Keeping the old resource would avoid a hard R4-to-R6 break, but it would also require R6 core and tooling to keep carrying a model HL7 may have decided not to maintain. Because the local inputs do not include official change notes, this is `Probably justified` rather than fully `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have left the R4 `ChargeItemDefinition` resource in core with deprecated or informational status and clear guidance not to use it for new designs. That would preserve most R4-valid instances, canonical resolution, package indexes, and generated classes. The material tradeoff is that deprecated resource shapes often persist indefinitely, and R6 would have to support a low-maturity definition resource alongside newer invoice, device, and monetary structures.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves validation and generated-type compatibility, but keeps a rough FMM 0 resource in core and risks indefinite parallel representations.

findings.narrativeMd: `ChargeItemDefinition` is not just renamed in the local R6 package; it is missing as a core StructureDefinition. That means the break occurs before individual element validation: R6 tooling cannot identify the resource type, load a profile, or build a native model class for it. Any existing R4 instances need an explicit migration policy rather than a schema-only upgrade.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `ChargeItemDefinition` instance becomes invalid or unprocessable in R6 core validation because there is no R6 base definition for the resource. R6-to-R4 representability is not directly applicable for this finding because there is no R6 `ChargeItemDefinition` content to convert back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all stored `ChargeItemDefinition` instances and canonical references. Decide whether to keep them in an R4 compatibility store, publish a custom R6 profile/extension package that preserves the resource-like content, or transform selected fields into other R6 financial structures. Tests should include resource-type recognition, canonical URL resolution, and server capability behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have been to retain the resource as deprecated or to provide an official compatibility package. That would avoid hard validation breaks but might conflict with an R6 design choice to remove low-maturity financial definition content from core.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Invoice`, `DeviceDefinition`, and `MonetaryComponent` were matched only by domain vocabulary and overlapping price/charge fields. The local package does not claim they are official successors to `ChargeItemDefinition`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The hard validation break is covered by the artifact-removal finding. This finding captures the migration risk: even after choosing another R6 structure, there is no obvious lossless target for reusable applicability rules or canonical definition metadata. That can force manual policy decisions and may change billing behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect migration of applicability rules can change when a charge or price component is considered valid, which is a business and compliance risk.

justification.inferredGoal: Move from a rough, profile-dependent definition resource toward charge and monetary data carried in more concrete financial contexts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a base R6 definitional resource, or a formal successor with applicability and propertyGroup semantics, instead of relying only on Invoice, DeviceDefinition, and MonetaryComponent surfaces.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving away from a rough, profile-dependent FMM 0 charge definition resource is a plausible R6 goal. A less-breaking base design could have preserved the reusable applicability and property-group model, but doing so would keep a second definitional representation next to the R6 invoice/device monetary structures and could confuse which representation is authoritative. With no official rationale or successor map in the local inputs, the break is only `Probably justified`, not conclusively justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A StructureMap, ConceptMap, extension package, or local sidecar strategy would be migration mitigation, not a backward-compatible base R6 design. The base-design alternative would be to retain `ChargeItemDefinition` or introduce a formal R6 successor that still carries canonical lifecycle metadata, definition-level applicability, group-level applicability, and grouped price components. That would preserve more R4 content, but the tradeoff is substantial: R6 would have both reusable definition semantics and invoice/device charge representations, and deprecated or duplicate representations can accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve reusable billing-rule semantics, but duplicates or competes with R6 transactional charge structures and retains a profile-dependent R4 model.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 CodeSystem has `base`, `surcharge`, `discount`, `tax`, and `informational`; it does not have a distinct `deduction` concept.

facts.note: R6 `discount` definition says it is sometimes referred to as a deduction.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `MonetaryComponent.type` is not an official ChargeItemDefinition successor, but its type/code/factor/amount shape closely matches R4 `priceComponent` and is used by R6 `Invoice` for price components.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a direct base-resource comparison because R6 has no `ChargeItemDefinition`. It becomes material if implementers map R4 `priceComponent` into R6 `MonetaryComponent`: an R4 component with `type: "deduction"` cannot be represented as the same required code in R6 and must be recoded, usually to `discount`, with potential semantic review.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The financial effect may remain a reduction if mapped to `discount`, but reports or analytics that distinguish deduction from discount can change.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify price component terminology by treating deduction as a discount-like reduction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `deduction` in the R6 `price-component-type` code system as a deprecated synonym of `discount` while making `discount` the preferred code.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The terminology simplification is understandable because the R6 `discount` definition explicitly says it may be referred to as a deduction. However, the same goal could likely have been met by retaining `deduction` as a deprecated or synonym code in the R6 required value set while preferring `discount` for new content. A ConceptMap alone would only be migration guidance, but preserving the code in the base R6 terminology would be a real less-breaking design, so this narrower terminology break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The base R6 alternative would add `deduction` to `price-component-type` with deprecation/synonym metadata and clear guidance that new instances should use `discount`. This would let migrated R4 price components remain code-preserving while still communicating the R6 simplification goal. The tradeoff is moderate terminology clutter: validators and analytics would need to normalize overlapping `discount` and `deduction` codes, and some systems might continue to treat them as distinct.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds some synonym-handling and analytics ambiguity, but preserves code-level migration with modest long-term cost.

findings.narrativeMd: The terminology issue is conditional on a chosen migration target. R4 distinguishes `deduction` from `discount`; the inspected R6 reusable monetary component type set does not. This can matter for billing analytics or local rules that treated the two reductions differently.

Test reducers that calculate totals and analytics that group by price component type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The least disruptive terminology design would keep `deduction` as a deprecated code or publish an official concept map. R6 instead appears to simplify the code set, which improves conceptual consistency but creates a migration decision for old data.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R6 terminology pages or ballot notes before treating `discount` as the only sanctioned target for all R4 deductions.

facts.newValue: No R6 core discriminator entry found

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Code generation and serialization impact follows directly from absence of the R6 computable definition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This finding is distinct from validation: applications may fail earlier at compile time or dispatch time because generated R6 libraries do not expose a `ChargeItemDefinition` model, parser case, route, search registry, or schema component. Dynamic FHIR stacks may still carry unknown JSON, but they cannot validate it as an R6 core resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If billing-definition content is dropped by serializers or rejected by APIs, downstream financial configuration can be lost.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid generating R6 support for a removed draft resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated core ChargeItemDefinition StructureDefinition so R6 generators can still emit a legacy resource model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The code generation and serializer break follows directly from removing the core resource. If retiring a draft, FMM 0 resource is accepted as the R6 design goal, then omitting generated support for that resource is probably justified. The alternative is less breaking but not low cost, because it requires R6 core generators, schemas, resource enums, and dispatch logic to keep supporting a resource that the base model no longer wants to expose.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A generated shim or external compatibility package is a useful mitigation but not a backward-compatible base R6 design. The base-design alternative would be to keep a deprecated `ChargeItemDefinition` StructureDefinition in the R6 core package so generators produce a legacy class and parser branch. That preserves source and runtime compatibility for many R4 applications, but it carries obsolete API surface indefinitely and can make it unclear whether accepting the resource is true R6 conformance or legacy tolerance.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces compile-time and parser breakage, but forces R6 core libraries to support an obsolete resource and blurs version-specific conformance.
